title: Promoting a healthy culture within engineering teams
description: An academic case study of engineering culture in an anonymized AI services company following an acquisition. It outlines a change approach informed by SWOT analysis, empathy maps, RASCI, and ADKAR.
abstract: Academic case study from 2023 on how to rebuild a healthier engineering culture after an acquisition. The case uses an anonymized B2B2C company that sells AI services and grew very quickly and reached more than 600 people in several countries. Leadership changes and departmental restructuring were followed by favoritism in promotions, technical decisions concentrated in a few people, little support for career development, less psychological safety, and people leaving. The study proposes a practical way to rebuild that culture. It looks at the maturity of technical leadership, how teams work together, and whether the environment is safe enough to learn. The suggested approach reads the situation with SWOT, empathy maps, RASCI, and system diagrams, then works on shared agreements, clearer career paths, and training in leadership and collaboration. The change itself is framed with the ADKAR model.

title: Adventure Works Cycles, a business intelligence project
description: An academic business intelligence project using the Adventure Works Cycles sample data. It covers an ETL pipeline, a star-schema data warehouse, and dashboards built with Power BI and Qlik Sense.
abstract: Academic business-intelligence project from 2018, built on the Adventure Works Cycles sample data, the fictional manufacturing and distribution company used in BI courses. The exercise looks at the distance between a complex transactional database and the questions a management team would ask when demand changes. I analyzed the sources, extracted and consolidated the data, and modeled a star schema around sales facts, with dimensions for customers, sales territories, and products. The result is a set of dashboards in Power BI and Qlik Sense for regional sales, customer segments, and descriptive forecasts. It is a course project on sample data, not a system delivered to a real company.

title: Circuitos, discover your artistic hub
description: A UX concept for a mobile product that helps people discover cultural events and routes around the city. The 2017 course project covered user research, product definition, and interface prototypes.
abstract: UX course concept from 2017 for a mobile product that helps people find cultural events and places in the city, such as design centers, local museums, and street art, when those schedules and spots are scattered. The concept has three parts. A local event list with personal scheduling, geolocated routes through curated cultural paths, and local storage for personal notes and favorites. I contributed to the research, the product concept, and the interface prototypes. It is a design concept from the course, not a shipped application.

title: Agent Orchestrator, a real-time AI telemetry dashboard
description: A real-time dashboard for monitoring the status and telemetry of simulated AI agents. Built with Vue 3, TypeScript, and Docker.

title: An idea for an application to promote cultural activities
description: A master's project developing a business case for a product that promotes cultural events in Barcelona. It includes market research, a business model, and a marketing plan.
type: e-Business Concept and Market Niche Analysis
abstract: Master's project from 2020, a business case for a digital product that would promote artistic and cultural events in Barcelona. It starts from the gap between general local listings and audiences looking for very specific kinds of culture. The case includes a market-entry analysis, with target audiences and competitors, a monetization model, and an online marketing plan with acquisition channels and operating indicators. Delivery is sketched as an agile timeline and a software stack kept inside a budget. It is a planning document for a concept, not a company that was launched.

title: TMDB catalog for movies and series
description: A full-stack web app for browsing a catalog of movies and TV series. It brings title information together in a straightforward interface.

title: Pokédex, gotta catch 'em all
description: A Svelte progressive web app that explores Pokémon data through the Pokémon API. It combines local data persistence, speech synthesis, and Plotly charts in a Pokédex experience.

title: Restaurant finder
description: A progressive web app that uses geolocation to help users find nearby restaurants. It is a discovery tool and does not support orders or delivery.

title: Visualization Dashboard for Monitoring
description: A D3.js dashboard for exploring error reports and other monitoring data through interactive charts. Users can switch between daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly views.

title: Management Dashboard
description: A web dashboard for managing employee information with create, read, update, and delete operations. The project demonstrates a focused CRUD workflow for team data.

title: Express API Backend Architecture
description: A starter structure for a small REST API using Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and Docker, with Jest and Supertest for testing. It is a reference project, not a production system.

title: Basic Sticky Notes
description: A browser-based board for creating, editing, moving, resizing, and deleting sticky notes. Changes are saved locally, and keyboard navigation supports use beyond pointer interactions.

title: Management System Pricing Calendar simulation with React, TypeScript, and TanStack Query
description: A revenue-management simulation for exploring rates on an interactive pricing calendar. It uses a decoupled full-stack architecture with an API server and reactive data flows.

title: Context-aware sticky note board with React, TypeScript, and Vite
description: An accessible board for capturing and organizing ideas with sticky notes. Create, edit, move, resize, and delete notes; group them into named contexts to filter the board or file notes. Notes and contexts are saved in the browser, with keyboard controls and screen-reader announcements supporting use beyond pointer interactions.

title: Semantic Graph CLI
description: A standalone TypeScript CLI for Engram that reads memory data from a local HTTP server and generates deterministic semantic graph snapshots in JSON. It supports project filtering, checks for stale observations, and publishes files atomically without changing the source data.

title: Type-safe GraphQL API (Domain-driven)
description: An in-progress GraphQL API built with TypeScript and Apollo Server, featuring end-to-end types, custom scalars, data loading, and generated documentation. An experimental natural-language query layer is also being explored; the project has not been released.

title: Cognitive Usability Analysis Tool
description: An experimental command-line tool that analyzes web interfaces through the lens of cognitive usability. It aims to identify friction points and opportunities to improve clarity, and is in early development.

title: Team-Memory-Health (TMH)
description: An agent-native CLI and skill for assessing the quality and alignment of a development team's shared memory. It examines coherence, freshness, coverage, and source distribution without scoring individuals or changing the data.
